UAE National Cybersecurity Strategy —
2025
Source status
The 2019 strategy previously stored in this file is outdated and has been superseded for
current-policy purposes. The UAE Cabinet approved a new National Cybersecurity Strategy
on 3 February 2025. The Head of the UAE Cyber Security Council announced on 11
February 2025, during the World Government Summit 2025, that the strategy would be
officially launched that week.
The current primary source is the UAE Cyber Security Council strategy document:
National Cyber Security Strategy — UAE Cyber Security Council, official document
The official document URL is retained above because the Cyber Security Council serves the
strategy document directly and the document is not rendered as HTML by the extraction
service. Do not use the former 2019 u.ae page as the current strategy source.
Official Cabinet announcement — 3 February 2025
The UAE Cabinet approved the National Cybersecurity Strategy. The Cabinet stated that the
strategy would continue strengthening cybersecurity measures, ensuring a resilient and
secure digital environment that protects national assets and supports future progress.
The Cabinet described the strategy as based on five main pillars:
1. Governance
2. Protection

3. Innovation
4. Establishing and building
5. Partnership
The strategy seeks to:
• Establish a cohesive and highly effective governance framework for cybersecurity.
• Ensure a secure, resilient, and sound digital environment.
• Enable the safe and swift adoption of innovations.
• Enhance national capabilities in digitization and cybersecurity.
• Bolster partnerships and collaborative relations at national and international levels.
Official Cabinet source
UAE Cabinet approves National Cybersecurity Strategy, API-First Policy — 3 February 2025
Official launch announcement — 11 February 2025
The Emirates News Agency reported that Dr. Mohamed Al Kuwaiti, Head of the UAE Cyber
Security Council, announced that the National Cybersecurity Strategy would be officially
launched during the week of the World Government Summit 2025.
The announcement states that the recently approved strategy is a five-year National
Cybersecurity Strategy endorsed by the UAE Cabinet. It is built around five key pillars
designed to enable the safe and rapid adoption of innovations while ensuring a secure,
resilient, and robust digital environment.
The announcement further states that the strategy includes specific goals and initiatives
aimed at strengthening and growing the national economy, in addition to protecting critical
infrastructure.
The Cyber Security Council also stated that it was finalising related policies and
cybersecurity standards to enhance institutional compliance and security measures.
Official launch source
UAE to launch National Cybersecurity Strategy — Emirates News Agency, 11 February
2025
Knowledge-base ingestion guidance
Use the Cyber Security Council document as the primary source for clause extraction. Use
the Cabinet and WAM announcements as corroborating official context for approval,

launch, timeframe, pillars, and high-level objectives.
For CascadeGuard, represent the following as strategy-level, non-legislative policy context
unless the primary document supplies a more specific binding mandate:
• governance : national cybersecurity governance and institutional coordination.
• protection : protection of the UAE digital environment and national assets.
• innovation : secure adoption of emerging technologies, including AI.
• establishing_and_building : national cybersecurity and digitization capabilities.
• partnership : national and international collaboration.
• critical_infrastructure : protection of critical infrastructure.
• incident_coordination : only create concrete reporting or response obligations when
supported by a clause in the Cyber Security Council document or another applicable
law or regulation.
Do not infer a legal deadline, regulator, reporting duty, or authority to disclose health or
telecom data from the five pillars alone. Those mappings require a specific cited provision
and human review.
Relationship to the old 2019 source
The former 2019 strategy page described five pillars, 60 initiatives, a National Cyber
Incident Response Plan, critical sectors, and a three-year period from June 2019. That
material may be retained separately as historical context, but it should not be loaded as the
current UAE National Cybersecurity Strategy for the 2025-era scenario.
Related current official source
For AI-specific cybersecurity requirements, also ingest the current official UAE page for the
National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence, established by the Cyber
Security Council and updated on 2 July 2026:
The National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence — official UAE Government
page
That policy covers governance, infrastructure and application security, algorithm security,
operational safety, adversarial AI attacks, and AI monitoring and response. It is
complementary to the national strategy and should be stored as a separate source, not
merged into this strategy record.
